notes.1: Bug: `namespace\` is not resolved as a relative name, the class `namespace\Foo` is read, and `App\namespace\Foo` inside the namespace `App`.
notes.2: By design: a name with a hyphen gives an error type, except the names of the `OCI-` classes.
notes.3: By design: a hyphen is reserved for the names of Psalm itself, an unknown name with a hyphen is rejected. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.4: Bug: `$this` is read as `static`, any instance of the called class, although the documentation tells them apart: "`@return static` is not enough: the method may return another instance of the class". Only `@return $this` alone keeps the object.

notes.4: Not implemented: a leading zero is not read, so there are no legacy octal numbers. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.5: Bug: the integer is cast from its text with `(int)` and becomes `0`. Fixed in phpdoc-parser 2.4.2, which normalizes integer literals, but PHPStan 2.3.7 still bundles 2.4.1.
notes.6: Not implemented: only decimal numbers are read. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.7: Not implemented: a float has no exponent. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.8: Not implemented: digit separators are read in integers only. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.

notes.10: Not implemented: a float needs a digit after the point, `.` becomes the description.

notes.12: Bug: the digits are cast to a 64-bit integer without a range check, and the value silently wraps to `-9223372036854775808`.

notes.14: Bug: the digits are cast to a 64-bit integer without a range check, and the value silently wraps to `9223372036854775807`.

notes.16: Not implemented: only one-character escapes such as `\n` are decoded in a double-quoted string, `\u{1F600}` stays as text.

notes.1: Not implemented: an offset access is read only as a template indexed by a template, `T[K]`. The parse tree reads `[...]` after a name as the purity brackets of `callable[pure]`, the type parser takes them as an offset only for a template name with a template inside.
notes.2: Not implemented: an offset access is read only as a template indexed by a template, `T[K]`.

notes.1: By design: `&` and `|` are not mixed without parentheses, phpstan#1877.
notes.2: By design: `?` is not combined with `|` or `&`, as in native PHP types, phpdoc-parser#321.
notes.3: Differs: Psalm reads `?(A&B)`, TypeLang reads `(?A)&B`, which is `A&B`. Neither reading is documented, PHPStan requires parentheses.
notes.4: Differs: `?` takes the whole type after it, mago reads `?(A&B)`, TypeLang reads `(?A)&B`, which is `A&B`. Neither reading is documented.
notes.5: Bug: the parse tree puts `?B` beside the intersection instead of inside it, and `B` is lost: `A|null` is returned instead of `(A&B)|null`.
notes.6: Bug: `B` is lost and `A&C` is returned, while `A&(B&C)` gives `A&B&C`.
notes.7: By design: the arrays of a union are merged into `array`, which also admits a mixed array `[A, B]`, the same way `array|array` is merged. The `[]` members are collected on purpose, for `Collection|Foo[]`, as the documentation describes.
notes.8: By design: the arrays of a union are merged into `array`, which also admits a mixed array `[A, B]`, for the projects that wrote `int[]|string[]` meaning either, psalm#5212.
notes.9: Not implemented: an intersection is kept only on a type that can carry one, an array cannot, so two arrays are rejected, while `iterable<A>&iterable<B>` and `A[]&iterable<B>` are read.
notes.10: Bug: the intersection collapses to `never` and loses `[]`, the one array of both, while `array<int&string>` gives `array<never>`.
notes.11: Bug: the parse tree puts `?B` beside the union instead of inside it, and `?B` is lost: `A[]` is returned, `(A|?B)` alone gives `A`.

notes.1: By design: the type of every parameter and the return type are required, as the PHPStan documentation says.
notes.2: Not implemented: only the postfix form `int...` is read, phpdoc-parser#125.
notes.3: Not implemented: only the postfix form `int...` is read, `...` is followed only by a name.
notes.4: Not implemented: `...` needs a type or a name after it.
notes.5: Not implemented: a parameter of a callable needs a type.
notes.6: Bug: a parameter without a type is read as the variable type `$a`, a reference to the parameter of the function, while `...$a` and `int $a` read `$a` as a name.
notes.7: Not implemented: `&` is read as a by-reference marker only after a type and before a name or `...`, otherwise it starts an intersection.
notes.8: Bug: the `&` is read as a dangling intersection and dropped, so the parameter is passed by value, as with `I1 & $x` in psalm#14874.
notes.9: Not implemented: only the bare optional marker `=` is read, not a default value.
notes.10: Bug: `$this` is read as `static`, any instance of the called class, although the documentation tells them apart: "`@return static` is not enough: the method may return another instance of the class". Only `@return $this` alone keeps the object.
notes.11: Not implemented: a conditional type is read only inside parentheses.
notes.12: By design: a conditional type is read only in parentheses, as the documentation says.
notes.13: By design: only `callable`, `Closure` and their variants take a parameter list, any other name with one gives an error type.
notes.14: Not implemented: a parameter list is read only after `callable`, `Closure` and their variants. The parse tree reads it as a method signature of `@method`, the type parser rejects it.
notes.15: Not implemented: a parameter list is read only after `callable`, `Closure` and their pure variants.
notes.16: Not implemented: in a docblock a space at the top level ends the type, except around `|` and `&` and before `{` and `:`, and the rest becomes the description. Such exceptions are added on request, psalm#10000.
notes.17: Differs: Psalm takes `T&U` as the return type, PHPStan and TypeLang read `(callable(): T)&U`. Neither reading is documented, Psalm itself ends the return type at `|`.
notes.18: Bug: `?T|U` is taken as the return type, while `callable(): T|U` is read as `(callable(): T)|U`.
notes.19: Bug: `?` takes the rest of the type, so `?T|U` becomes the return type, while `callable(): T|U` is read as `(callable(): T)|U`.
notes.20: Not implemented: a callable as a return type is read only inside parentheses, `callable(): (callable(): T)`.
notes.21: Bug: Psalm reads `callable(): ((callable(): T)|U)`, the `|` leaves only the inner callable, while `callable(): T|U` is read as `(callable(): T)|U`.

notes.4: Not implemented: the sign belongs to the number token, a space after it is not read.

notes.6: Not implemented: `...<>` takes a key type and a value type, a single one is an open request, psalm#13774. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.7: Bug: a single argument of `...<>` is taken as the key type and the value becomes `mixed`, while `array<string>` and `list{...<string>}` take it as the value type.
notes.8: Not implemented: no shape after `non-empty-array`, an open request, psalm#13774. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.
notes.9: Not implemented: `...` is read only in array and list shapes.
notes.10: Not implemented: the key of an object shape is a name or a quoted string only.

notes.12: Not implemented: a shape is read only after `array`, `list`, `object` and `callable-array`. The parse tree keeps it, the type parser rejects it.

notes.9: Not implemented: it is read as `string`, which also admits a lower case string. The alias was suggested as a first step in psalm#11227, the type itself is a TODO in the source and an open request, psalm#13774.
notes.10: By design: it is read as `resource`, which also admits a closed one, resources are not worth the effort as PHP moves away from them, phpstan#13295.

notes.1: Bug: a dangling operator is ignored.
notes.2: Accepted: a dangling `|` before the end or a closing bracket is a dedicated `TrailingPipe` node of the tree, and the type is read without it.
notes.3: Bug: the doubled `&` is read as one.
notes.4: Bug: the doubled `?` is read as one.
notes.5: Accepted: `?` applies to any type, a nullable one too, and `?(?int)` is read.
notes.6: Bug: `?[]` after the type is dropped.
notes.7: Bug: the `*` after a space is stripped as a docblock margin.
notes.8: Bug: the space between a name and `*` is skipped and `PHP_*` is read, while `int *` leaves `*` in the description.
notes.9: Bug: the second string is dropped.
notes.10: Accepted: a name may hold any run of backslashes.
notes.11: Accepted: a name may hold `-` after its first character, for names such as `non-empty-string`, and nothing forbids it at the end.
notes.12: Accepted: a name may hold `-` anywhere after its first character, for names such as `non-empty-string`, and nothing forbids it at the end.
notes.13: Accepted: digits after a leading zero are read as a decimal number, PHP rejects `08`.
notes.14: Accepted: a leading zero followed by `8` or `9` is read as a decimal number, PHP rejects `08`.
notes.15: Accepted: the integer rule allows doubled digit separators, PHP rejects them.
notes.16: Accepted: a digit separator may follow the decimal point, PHP rejects it. Reported in phpdoc-parser#343, not confirmed.
notes.17: Bug: `::class` after a constant is dropped.
notes.19: Accepted: a constant name may hold `-`. Reported in phpdoc-parser#343, not confirmed.
notes.20: Accepted: a constant name is lexed as a name, which may hold `-`.
notes.21: By design: `T of Bar` is the template map syntax of Psalm, as in `class-string-map<T of Foo, T>`.
notes.22: Bug: the type after `...` is dropped and the shape is read as open.
notes.23: Accepted: the text of an unquoted key is not checked and becomes a string key.
